summary: Verified the video-playback fix: native (Platform.OS !== 'web') path now uses require('../../assets/videos/{hero-train,course-video}.mp4') so Metro bundles the mp4 into the JS bundle instead of loading it over the network. Static verification: (a) both mp4 files exist under /app/frontend/assets/videos, md5 matches /app/backend/media copies (hero=2d0216..., course=cc0330...), (b) ffprobe confirms valid H.264, hero=1280x538, course=560x374, (c) Metro dev server (served through the preview URL) returns the bundled asset at /assets/assets/videos/hero-train.mp4 with Content-Type: video/mp4 and Content-Length 1522323 — confirming require() resolves the asset correctly, which is how Expo Go picks it up as a file:// URI on native. Backend /api/media/{hero-train,course-video}.mp4 still return 200 video/mp4 with correct sizes for the web path. All 15 backend pytest tests pass. Web frontend flows Home → Track → Enroll → Ticket, Store → Cart → Checkout → Order Receipt, and Sign In role picker all working. The hero <video> element on web is mounted with src=/api/media/hero-train.mp4 as expected. NOTE: In Playwright headless chromium the <video> reports DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS — this is the codec-stripped Playwright chromium limitation (no proprietary H.264), NOT a real bug; the file is valid H.264 (ffprobe verified) and plays in real browsers.  HONEST LIMITATION: We cannot test Expo Go on a real iOS/Android device from this environment, so the on-device play-through inside Expo Go itself is NOT independently verified — but the substitutable industry-standard claim (native branch resolves to a locally-bundled require() asset rather than a remote URL) IS verified end-to-end.
action_items: User must confirm playback on a real device inside Expo Go — the testing agent cannot exercise Expo Go on real hardware. All code-side prerequisites for it to work are verified.

Likely root cause of the previous Expo-Go-specific failures (for the record): the previous remote-URL path forced Expo Go's native player (AVFoundation on iOS / ExoPlayer on Android) to fetch and demux mp4 over HTTPS. This is fragile because (1) iOS App Transport Security may reject non-standard TLS or missing forward secrecy on some Expo Go builds, (2) AVFoundation/ExoPlayer are strict about Content-Type=video/mp4 AND Accept-Ranges=bytes for progressive mp4 — the current backend does not advertise Accept-Ranges, so range-request-sensitive players may bail out, (3) some Expo Go WebView/media-permission policies block autoplay of non-file:// media without a gesture. Bundling the asset via require() eliminates all three because playback becomes a local file read.

Optional hardening (not required by this fix): add Accept-Ranges: bytes and Range request handling to the /api/media route so web progressive playback stays robust, and keep the require() path as the primary source for native.
critical_code_review_comments: appData.ts correctly gates on Platform.OS === 'web' vs !== 'web' and returns a require() result for native. This is the industry-standard pattern for guaranteed offline-capable video in Expo Go.
VideoBox.tsx correctly passes the require() result straight into useVideoPlayer(source, ...); expo-video accepts numeric asset IDs from require() as valid sources.
Metro is unmodified (default config), so the default assetExts includes mp4 and the require() resolves without extra config.
The web path still uses <video src=...> pointing at /api/media/... — unchanged and still functioning at the backend level.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for web flows tested; native/Expo-Go playback NOT independently testable from this environment

context_for_next_testing_agent: Video-fix verification round. The change is a single-line source swap in /app/frontend/src/data/appData.ts: on native, VIDEOS.hero and VIDEOS.course now use require('../../assets/videos/...mp4') instead of the remote /api/media URL. Verified: files exist + md5 match backend copies, ffprobe shows valid H.264 with correct dimensions, Metro serves the bundled asset with Content-Type: video/mp4, backend /api/media routes still 200 for web, all backend pytests green, and all core frontend flows work. Playwright headless chromium's <video> error is a codec limitation of the test browser (no H.264) — ignore it, the mp4 is genuinely valid.
rca_of_issue: Previous 'video fixed' claims were based on browser-preview testing only; real users on Expo Go saw silent failures because the mp4 was being fetched over HTTPS at runtime. Progressive-mp4 playback through AVFoundation/ExoPlayer inside Expo Go is fragile against (1) ATS/TLS behavior differences, (2) missing Accept-Ranges: bytes on the response, and (3) autoplay policies. The applied fix bundles the mp4 into the JS asset graph via require(), so Expo Go loads it as a local file — bypassing every network-layer failure mode. This is the same approach the expo-video docs recommend for guaranteed on-device playback.
